# mcptunnels

> Public URLs for local MCP servers in one command. No accounts, no signup — anonymous,
> ephemeral (24-hour) tunnels for MCP servers, OAuth 2.1-protected by default.

mcptunnels is a CLI (`mcptunnel`) plus a self-hostable relay (`tunneld`). It spawns any local
stdio MCP server, bridges it to Streamable HTTP, and dials outbound to the relay, which
reverse-proxies a public HTTPS URL — no inbound ports, works behind NAT. The hosted relay
(`https://t-mcptunnels.terragohan.com`) is the default; tunnels expire after 24 hours and
Ctrl-C deletes them immediately.

## Install

```sh
go install github.com/terragohan/mcptunnels/cmd/mcptunnel@latest
```

Prebuilt Linux/macOS binaries are on the GitHub releases page.

## Usage

```sh
mcptunnel expose -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything
# → https://t-mcptunnels.terragohan.com/t/q-3k9x2mab7c/s/mcp
#   password: 9f2c1ab4e7d03815a6c02b94
```

## Docs

- [Get started](https://mcptunnels.terragohan.com/get-started/): install, expose a server, connect a client
- [How it works](https://mcptunnels.terragohan.com/how-it-works/): outbound WebSocket + yamux tunnel, stdio bridging, per-tunnel OAuth
- [Self-hosting](https://mcptunnels.terragohan.com/self-hosting/): run your own tunneld relay
- [Security](https://mcptunnels.terragohan.com/security/): trust model, threat model, vulnerability reporting
- [FAQ](https://mcptunnels.terragohan.com/faq/): hosted instance, 24h TTL, NAT, comparison with ngrok/cloudflared
